sandbox_argv:
This exploration produces ONE mechanism. You are one of three independent reviewers; you see the same frozen evidence bundle and the same proposals as the others, and you do not coordinate with them before handing in.
THE RESEARCH OBJECTIVE:
Discover new mechanisms in which TRAINING-ONLY user behaviour and HYPERBOLIC geometry are computationally coupled to improve the RQ-VAE Semantic IDs used by a generative next-item recommender, with the real target of Stage3 test Recall@10 above 0.065.
THE SCOPE CONTRACT (a proposal that misses it is sent back, not scored):
A proposal is IN SCOPE only when all of this holds:
  1. BEHAVIOUR: it names one training-only behaviour signal (directed item transitions, user-interest branching, sequential co-consumption, popularity-adjusted graph neighbours, behaviour-conditioned assignment weights, ...) and says how it is computed.
  2. HYPERBOLIC GEOMETRY: it names an explicit curved operation (trainable or fixed negative curvature, Poincare or Lorentz distance, exp/log maps, geodesic scoring, curved residual, curved quantization, curved regularization) and where in training or quantization it acts.
  3. REAL COUPLING: one connected computational pathway uses both, so that removing either changes the core computation. A behaviour suffix on an unchanged Euclidean quantizer, a standalone hyperbolic loss beside an unrelated behaviour loss, a geometry name without geometric computation, or inherited unused hyperbolic code do NOT qualify.
  4. TESTABLE EFFECT: it states what should observably change (SID assignment, gradient or parameter update, prefix behaviour predictability, or Stage3 Recall) and names the behaviour-off, geometry-off/Euclidean and both-on comparisons. The three switches must be part of the mechanism, so that the coupling can be shown to be real, but the round RUNS no ablation arm: each candidate is trained once.
  5. MINIMAL SPECIFICATION: equations or pseudocode, inputs and outputs, numerical safeguards and the training cost. No proof and no paper section are required.
SID quality (ER, prefix counts, collisions) is NOT a scope criterion and NOT an admission rule.

EXPERIMENT POLICY (binding on every proposal, implementation and review):
  - ONE candidate, ONE training run, on the frozen budget (3000 Stage 2 epochs on four cards, the frozen Stage 3 protocol, no early stopping).
  - NO ablation experiments: the behaviour-off, geometry-off and both-on switches must EXIST in the code and must be correct, but no arm is trained with them switched off.
  - NO tuning experiments: no sweep over the coupling weight, the clip bound, the temperature, the usage weight or any other constant. A constant that enters the mechanism has to be DERIVED (a scale-relative bound, a measured quantity, a documented default), not chosen by trying values.
  - NO multi-seed experiments: a candidate is not repeated with other seeds, so a single run decides it and the seed noise is part of the uncertainty.
  - The behavioural diagnostics (coherence, adjacency, transfer predictability) are recorded, never used as an admission gate; Stage 3 test_recall@10 is the judgement.
  - A proposal that needs an ablation, a sweep or a seed repetition to make its case is out of programme: it has to make the case with one run.
THE SELECTION POLICY (rank-2026-10-v1): the reviewers RANK the proposals. The proposal the reviewers place best, in total, is the round's mechanism. Rank every proposal, best first, and give each one a reason that names the evidence you used.
Read the frozen evidence bundle for each proposal before you place it: a placement you cannot ground in the evidence is not a placement.
Write PLAIN TEXT, one line per proposal, in exactly this shape:
RANK: <idea_id> | position=<1 for the best, then 2, 3, ...> | reason=<one line>
RANK: <idea_id> | position=<n> | reason=<one line>
Every proposal must appear exactly once, the positions must be 1..N with no ties and no gaps, and the reason must say what in the evidence put the proposal there. If you cannot ground a proposal in the evidence, rank it last and say so in its reason; do not leave a proposal out.
THE PROPOSALS:
IDEA: QPEX-CURVBIAS
TITLE: Quota-preserving SID exchange under an additive, standardised-curvature Poincare proximity bias
MOTIVATION: The two measured failures are (i) a multiplicative behaviour weight on a Euclidean distance that moved margins but moved no arg-min, and (ii) a codebook whose radius was spent on curvature, collapsing support to 56 triples. What is missing is an assignment mechanism in which the behaviour-curvature signal is ADDITIVE on the cost (so it provably reorders the top-1), the per-level usage multiset is EXACT by construction (so the resolution cannot collapse), and the curvature is spent only as a signed re-ranking pressure, never as a radius.
NOVELTY: Earlier arms either (a) made curvature set a level/ball scale (CURVCTRL-SID, BRad-RQ, Poincare-Frechet codebook), (b) multiplied a distance by a behaviour weight (CURVCAP-SUCCPLAN), or (c) used a transport plan whose arg-max need not reproduce its marginals. This proposal uses a swap-exact assignment whose invariant is the Euclidean code histogram, and injects the training-split standardised curvature deviation as a zero-mean additive bias times a fixed-curvature Poincare distance held outside the gradient. Removing the behaviour zeroes the bias and the rule provably returns the Euclidean assignment (verified as Hamming 0); removing the curvature replaces d_P by a Euclidean tangent distance on the same ball. Nothing here rescales a code, a ball or a codebook radius.
CHANGE: Inside each RQ level, compute the normal Euclidean cost C_ik and the Euclidean assignment a0 with code histogram m_k; then add b_ik = lambda_l * delta_l * d_P(u_i, v_k) (centred over k) to the cost and run a fixed number of count-preserving item-code SWAPS starting from a0. The output digit vector has exactly the histogram m_k of the Euclidean argmin, and its digits differ from a0 for a measured set of items.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': "(1) Pre-pass on the TRAINING split only: build the weighted quotient transition graph W^l_{jk} by counting training item transitions s_t -> s_{t+1} between the level-l codes j,k of the initial Euclidean codebooks; compute Ollivier-Ricci curvature kappa_e per edge with lazy random walk m_j = 0.5*delta_j + 0.5*W_j./deg_j and d = graph shortest path, kappa_e = 1 - W1(m_j,m_k)/d(j,k); take kappa_hat_l = mean_e kappa_e. (2) Null: R=20 size-preserving member shuffles (permute item->code membership inside each level keeping each code's item count), recompute kappa_hat_l each time; z_l = (kappa_hat_l - mean_null)/sd_null; delta_l = z_l - mean_{l'=1..3} z_{l'}; clip |delta_l| to 1.0. On the frozen baseline this reproduces delta = [-0.328, -0.071, +0.399]. (3) Save delta and a per-level lambda_l to the run config; every rank loads the same file. (4) Per training step (batch of n~1023 items), per level l=1..3 with residual r_i and code c_k: u_i = tanh(||r_i||/2) r_i/||r_i||; v_k = tanh(||c_k||/2) c_k/||c_k|| (both stop-gradient); d_P(u,v) = arcosh(1 + 2||u-v||^2 / ((1-||u||^2)(1-||v||^2) + 1e-9)); C_ik = ||r_i - c_k||^2; a0_i = argmin_k C_ik; m_k = count(a0 = k); lambda_l = median_i(C_{i,a1}-C_{i,a2}) / median_{i,k} d_P (measured once at epoch 0, frozen); b_ik = lambda_l * delta_l * (d_P(u_i,v_k) - mean_k d_P(u_i,v_k)). (5) T=1 sweep (documented default) in a seed-fixed item order: for item i at code j, for each non-empty bucket k != j, let i* = argmax_{i' in bucket k} (C_{i',k}+b_{i',k}); swap i and i* iff (C_ik+b_ik)+(C_{i*,j}+b_{i*,j}) < (C_ij+b_ij)+(C_{i*,k}+b_{i*,k}); update the two buckets. The bucket sizes are never changed, so the histogram is the invariant. (6) Commit digits, form residuals r_i <- r_i - c_{a_i}, keep the baseline reconstruction + commitment loss and the baseline EMA codebook update unchanged. (7) At SID construction time for any split (including Stage 3 items) the same frozen delta, lambda, codebooks and swap rule are applied; test items bring embeddings only, no behaviour."}
COST: Offline: quotient graphs have <=256 nodes per level; 3 levels x 21 curvature evaluations (1 real + 20 nulls), Sinkhorn 50 iterations ~ 3.3e6 ops each, plus one pass over 24556 residuals x 256 x 3 for the margins: under 1-2 min on one GPU (or a few minutes CPU), executed before Stage 2, outside the training loop. Per step at the frozen scale (n~1023 items, K=256, L=3): 3 x 262k Poincare distances (~20 flops each) = ~16 MFLOP plus 3 x (262k cost entries + 2 x 262k exchange comparisons) ~ 2.4M scalar ops, i.e. roughly +5 to +15 percent step time over the baseline RQ forward/backward; ~+0.2 to +1 s per epoch, ~+10 to +50 min over the 3000-epoch run. No extra epochs, no extra forward passes.
HYPOTHESIS: If delta_l>0 means the level's behaviour quotient is more clustered than its size-preserving null, then a positive bias on d_P (penalising codes far from the item in the Poincare ball) reinforces the clusters the behaviour graph already shows, while delta_1<0 (fine level under-curved) pushes the fine digit away from hyperbolic proximity, i.e. separates items that the null says are not neighbours. If the coarse digit becomes more behaviourally predictable from its prefix, the frozen Stage 3 beam should find the right level-3 group more often, and test_recall@10 should exceed the baseline 0.055537 and approach 0.065, while the per-level histograms, the 247/7414/20223 supports and the 0.177 collision are unchanged by construction.
RISKS: ['The sign of the curvature deviation may be the wrong direction for recall and, with no tuning allowed, a single run loses; the bias is calibrated to the median top-2 margin so it only touches the ambiguous half of the assignment and the effect may be under one point of recall; tanh projection saturates for large residual norms, making d_P nearly constant and the coupling weak; one sweep of swaps may stop in a poor local optimum; the offline curvature is computed on the epoch-0 codebooks and goes stale as the codebook moves; exact quota preservation can still raise triple collisions if the swaps concentrate items, so the collision rate must be watched.']
END IDEA

IDEA: EQVOTE-HYP-RQ
TITLE: Exact-quota hyperbolic vote assignment: an additive curvature-kernel behaviour bias that permutes RQ slots without ever touching the usage multiset
MOTIVATION: The baseline TIGER_RQ-VAE (247/7414/20223, Stage3 test_recall@10 = 0.055537) clusters items purely by content, so a fine (level-3) token says "this item looks like these items" and not "this item sits on this behavioural branch". The generative model therefore has to guess branch identity from content evidence alone. Round 1 tried to fix this by spending the measured behaviour-graph curvature on the SID space radius and the codebook collapsed (170 -> 56 distinct triples, recall 0.041888); round 2 tried to fix it with a multiplicative per-pair cost weight and the verifier measured 0 of 4 argmins moving. The problem is real (the level-3 behaviour quotient is more tree-like than its size-preserving null, delta_3 = +0.399) but it needs a mechanism whose top-1 effect is provable and whose capacity effect is zero.
NOVELTY: Three things that no earlier arm here did. (i) The behaviour term is a bounded PROBABILITY-like vote, not a distance rescale: v(i,c) in [0,1], so its top-1 effect is an absolute cost gap rather than a ratio gap and cannot be a no-op on non-equidistant codes. (ii) The assignment object is not a soft plan and not a radius: quotas are read off the Euclidean pass and then the labelling is changed only by composing transpositions of two items' labels, so the per-level usage multiset is invariant BY CONSTRUCTION with nothing to assert about marginals. (iii) The curvature is spent INSIDE the kernel metric used to spread the vote (curvature nu_l = exp(delta_l) on R-normalised coordinates), so it changes which codeword a behaviour vote lands on while leaving codebook vectors, radii and counts untouched; and the sign-gated strength s_l = [delta_l]_+ / sum [delta_l]_+ spends it only where the measured quotient is genuinely above its null, which on the evidence is level 3 alone.
CHANGE: At each RQ level the Euclidean residual argmin is computed first and its per-codeword counts are frozen as quotas; every training successor of item i then casts a weight w_ij at the level-l codeword it currently occupies, that vote is spread over codewords by a Poincare kernel exp(-d_P(v_l)^2/2) evaluated at curvature exp(delta_l) on R-normalised codebook coordinates, and the negated vote enters the assignment cost as an ADDITIVE term whose magnitude is the level's own measured median reconstruction distortion. The item-to-codeword labelling is then improved by accepted transpositions only, so the Euclidean usage multiset is reproduced exactly.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': "Notation: level l in {1,2,3}; codebook E_l = {e_c}, c = 1..256; r_{l-1}(i) is the level-l input residual; R = median_i ||x_i|| over the 24556 training content embeddings (offline, one scalar).\nOffline constants (a 3-vector shipped in the config): delta_l = kappa_hat_l - mean_l(kappa_hat_l), where kappa_hat_l is the edge-weight-weighted mean of the null-standardised Ollivier curvatures of the training behaviour quotient at the frozen baseline SIDs' level-l prefixes. On the measured evidence delta = [-0.328, -0.071, +0.399].\nPer step, per level l (levels with s_l = 0 are skipped entirely and are bit-identical to the baseline):\n1. Euclidean pass: cE(i) = argmin_c ||r_{l-1}(i) - e_c||^2; quotas q(c) = |{i in batch : cE(i) = c}|.\n2. Ball map: nu_l = exp(delta_l); z_c = exp_0^{nu_l}(e_c / R), with exp_0^nu(v) = tanh(sqrt(nu)||v||/2) v/||v||.\n3. Kernel: Khat[c,c'] = exp( -d_P^{nu_l}(z_c, z_c')^2 / 2 ), distances in R units.\n4. Successor vote: v(i,c) = sum_{j in N+(i)} w_ij Khat[c, c_l^cache(j)] / sum_{j in N+(i)} w_ij, and v(i,c) = 0 if N+(i) is empty; c_l^cache is the previous-epoch-end level-l Euclidean code of j.\n5. Additive cost: S(i,c) = ||r_{l-1}(i) - e_c||^2 - lambda_l * v(i,c), with lambda_l = s_l * median_i ||r_{l-1}(i) - e_{cE(i)}||^2.\n6. Quota-exact permutation by swap local search (T = 3 passes, no cap on accepted swaps): described in SPEC EQUATIONS.\n7. The final labelling drives the usual codebook EMA/update; the geometry and the kernel are detached (no gradient through the hyperbolic map)."}
COST: Only level 3 executes (s = [0,0,1] on the evidence). Added per step at 1023 x 256 x 32: cost matrix 8.4 MFLOP, codebook kernel 256x256x32 = 2.1 MFLOP, sparse vote 1023x16x256 = 4.2 MFLOP, three swap passes ~1.6 MFLOP, total ~16 MFLOP per step against the baseline's level-3 assignment of ~8.4 MFLOP, i.e. 2-3x the RQ-VAE assignment work and roughly 1.4-2x Stage-2 wall clock over 3000 epochs x 24 steps = 72,000 steps (tens of minutes, four cards). Epoch-boundary residual cache refresh over all 24556 items is 0.4 GFLOP per epoch, 1.2 TFLOP total, minutes. Offline curvature precompute: transition graph a few million edges, Ollivier W1 per edge under 32 member-shuffle draws, a few minutes to ~20 minutes once on CPU. Memory +0.3 MB (batch x C plus C x C). Stage 3 is untouched and runs the frozen protocol.
HYPOTHESIS: Worth keeping iff (i) the vote materially reorders the fine level - frac_top1_changed_3 between roughly 0.08 and 0.30 with levels 1 and 2 at exactly 0 - and (ii) that reordering raises the fine-token conditional predictability of the true next item without raising collisions. Observed as: distinct-triple count stays near 7414 (it cannot fall below the baseline level-1 pattern because that level is bit-identical), first-level hit rates stay at 0.079/0.005, collision near 0.177, and Stage3 test_recall@10 > 0.055537 with 0.065 as the target. If frac_top1_changed_3 is under 0.02 the coupling is present but inert and the idea is dead regardless of recall.
RISKS: ["(1) Co-consumed items are content-similar, so the vote may mostly agree with the Euclidean argmin and few swaps survive the cost test - the mechanism becomes a no-op and recall is unchanged. (2) Because the cost test includes the Euclidean distortion, the swaps may concentrate on poorly reconstructed, low-margin items and change nothing that matters. (3) The level-3-only gate makes the effect small: one token of three changes for a minor fraction of items, so even a correct mechanism may only move recall by a few thousandths. (4) The hyperbolic kernel may be numerically close to the Euclidean kernel for codewords at similar radii, making the geometry-off arm nearly identical to both-on; this is the specific comparison that must be reported, not assumed. (5) Successor votes taken from the previous epoch's cache lag by up to 24 steps and could reinforce an early accident."]
END IDEA

IDEA: CURVQUOTA-SWAP-SID
TITLE: Curvature-biased, quota-exact 2-swap code assignment for a Poincare-ball RQ-VAE
MOTIVATION: The baseline TIGER RQ-VAE gives every training item the code triple nearest to it in an isotropic Euclidean residual space, so a SID carries no information about where the item sits in the training transition graph, and two items users actually consume in sequence frequently get different prefixes. Round 1 spent the measured behaviour-graph curvature on the space's radius and destroyed the codebook (170 -> 56 distinct triples, Stage3 recall 0.041888). Round 2 put behaviour in as a multiplicative per-pair weight: margins moved, not one argmin did. What is missing is a behaviour term that provably changes which code an item receives, plus a resolution guarantee that survives any curved metric, however aggressive.
NOVELTY: The assignment is constrained to be a PERMUTATION of the Euclidean nearest-neighbour assignment of the same batch shard: a sequence of transpositions. The per-level usage multiset is therefore invariant by construction (every code keeps exactly the count the baseline quantizer gave it, so collision rate and exposure are unchanged), while WHICH item holds which code is re-decided by an additive curved-plus-curvature cost. No Sinkhorn plan, no marginal argmax, no rescaling of distances, no radius, temperature or usage-weight parameter, no codebook renormalisation. The behaviour-graph curvature is spent as an additive per-pair cost term and never as a scale.
CHANGE: (1) Encoder outputs and code vectors are mapped into the unit Poincare ball, the quantization distance becomes d_P at fixed curvature c=1, and the codebook EMA is carried in the tangent space at the origin. (2) Inside each level and each rank-local batch shard, the code of item i is chosen by a cost that adds a curvature-weighted successor-mass bias to the normalised curved distance, and that cost is minimised by exact 2-swaps starting from the Euclidean nearest assignment, so the multiset can never move.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': "Offline, once, on CPU before Stage 2 (no collectives, one artifact memory-mapped by all ranks):\n  1. w_ij = directed transition counts over TRAIN-split sequences only, i,j in the 24556 training items.\n  2. pi_l(i) = level-l prefix of training item i under the FROZEN baseline RQ-VAE (train items only).\n  3. Quotient graph per level: W_l(a,b) = sum over i with pi_l(i)=a and j with pi_l(j)=b of w_ij.\n  4. Per edge (a,b) with W_l>0, Ollivier curvature with the alpha=0.5 lazy random walk:\n     kappa_l(a,b) = 1 - W1(a,b)/d(a,b), W1 = sum_{u,v} mu_a(u) mu_b(v) d(u,v),\n     mu_a(u) = alpha*1[u=a] + (1-alpha)*W_l(a,u)/deg_l(a), d = unweighted shortest path on the quotient.\n  5. Null: S=32 size-preserving member shuffles; each shuffle reassigns items to prefixes drawn without replacement from the list in which each prefix appears n_a times, so the prefix-size multiset is preserved; kappa is recomputed on a FIXED sample of 2000 edges per level per shuffle and all values are pooled into mu_l, sigma_l.\n  6. kappa_hat_l(a,b) = clip((kappa_l(a,b) - mu_l)/sigma_l, -4, +4); kappa_bar_l = mean over quotient edges;\n     delta_l = kappa_bar_l - mean_l'(kappa_bar_l'); eta_l = delta_l / std_l'(delta_l').\n  7. Artifact acceptance check: |kappa_bar_l - [-2.32,-1.80,-0.86]_l| <= 0.15 for all three levels, otherwise abort.\n  Training loop, per step, per level l=1..3, per rank's local shard (no cross-rank call anywhere):\n      x_i = phi(h_i), e_k = phi(theta_k), phi(z) = z/(1+||z||) so ||x||<1\n      D[i,k] = d_P(x_i, e_k)\n      a0[i] = argmin_k ||x_i - e_k||          # Euclidean nearest: quota reference (baseline quantizer's own choice)\n      q[k] = |{i : a0[i] = k}|                # the protected multiset, exactly\n      Bias[i,k] = eta_l * kappa_hat_l(a0[i], k) * w_i(k)/w_i, on item i's successor-code support, zero elsewhere\n      C[i,k] = D[i,k]/m_l + Bias[i,k]\n      a <- a0; for round = 1..12 (documented default):\n          M[i,k] = C[i,k] - C[i,a[i]]                       # regret of moving i to k\n          A[p,r] = min over {i : a[i]=p} of M[i,r]          # scatter-amin, O(B*K)\n          G[p,r] = A[p,r] + A[r,p]                          # best 2-swap gain between codes p and r\n          (p*,r*) = argmin G; if G[p*,r*] < 0, swap the two argmin items, else leave\n      commit a[i]; residual r_i <- r_i - e_{a[i]}; proceed to level l+1\n  Loss: curved commitment d_P(x,e)^2 with stop-gradient on the code, plus the reconstruction term unchanged.\n  Codebook: t_k <- (1-gamma) t_k + gamma * mean_{i assigned to k} log_0(x_i); e_k = exp_0(t_k), gamma = 0.99 baseline default."}
COST: Per step at the frozen scale (24556 training items, 24 steps per epoch, 3000 epochs = 72000 steps): 3 levels x 1024 x 256 = 786k Poincare distance evaluations, about 16 MFLOP, plus 3 x 12 rounds x (B*K + K*K) roughly 12 MFLOP, plus three host synchronisations to read the fixed-round result, so about 3-6 ms per step on an A100-class card, roughly 5-10% over the baseline step, about 6 minutes of added wall clock over the whole run. Memory: artifact 20-30 MB, memory-mapped, no per-rank copy. Offline build: one CPU pass over training sequences plus 32 shuffles x 3 levels x 2000 sampled edges, 25-45 minutes once, outside the four-card Stage 2 budget.
HYPOTHESIS: That the standardised behaviour-graph curvature of a level identifies which successor codes a code should be allowed to reach, so reallocating items between codes under that additive bias places co-transitioning items in shared prefixes more often without moving a single usage count. If true: the per-level swap rate is non-zero at levels 1 and 3 and near zero at level 2; prefix-bigram top-1 accuracy of level 2 given level 1 and of level 3 given levels 1-2 rises against the same model with the bias off; distinct prefix counts stay near 247/7414/20223 and the collision rate stays near 0.177 because the multiset is invariant; and Stage 3 test_recall@10 exceeds 0.065 against the 0.055537 baseline. If the swap rate is below about 1% at every level, the hypothesis is already false at the assignment and the recall result is interpretable without further experiments.
RISKS: ["eta_2 is small (-0.24), so the middle level may barely move and a third of the mechanism may be inert; the quotient is built on the frozen baseline's prefixes and is therefore a static prior that can drift from the codebook being trained; the 12-round budget may bind and leave the descent far from its local optimum; the Poincare metric concentrates distances near the boundary and, although the quota forbids collapse, it may still push unrelated items into rare codes and hurt prefix predictability; the bias magnitude (eta * kappa_hat * successor mass, typically 0.1-0.4 against a normalised distance spread near 1) may be too small to move enough items, in which case the measured swap rate is exactly the diagnostic that says so."]
END IDEA

IDEA: geopull-exactquota
TITLE: Geodesic successor pull with capacity-exact (quota-preserving) deferred-acceptance SID assignment
MOTIVATION: The round-1 arm spent curvature on the radius of the latent ball and the codebook collapsed from 170 to 56 distinct triples (recall 0.0419, below its own parent). The round-2 arm multiplied the transport cost by a per-pair behaviour weight; margins moved but not one arg-min did, so the behaviour dependency was uncertifiable, and its frozen plan did not reproduce its column marginals. The real problem is therefore not "more curvature" but: get behaviour into the arg-min as an ADDITIVE, order-changing term, and protect the per-level usage multiset EXACTLY rather than approximately. Recommendation-wise, what is missing in TIGER SIDs is that two items a user actually jumps between often land in different coarse prefixes, which destroys prefix-level next-item predictability.
NOVELTY: (i) The codebook is never moved and never re-parameterised: the curved operation acts only on the discrete assignment, so curvature cannot act as a radius/scale on the codebook. (ii) The curvature is spent as a DIRECTION and DISTANCE ALONG A GEODESIC set by the measured, null-standardised behaviour-graph curvature, not as a metric scale: kappa is fixed at 1 and delta_l only sets the geodesic fraction t_l. (iii) The assignment is a capacity-constrained deferred-acceptance (many-to-one Gale-Shapley) allocation whose output has the Euclidean per-level usage multiset EXACTLY by counting, not by a plan's arg-max - this is the direct answer to failure (b). (iv) Unlike the round-1 successor-Frechet codebook update, the successor Frechet mean here is a per-item additive bias on a quota-exact integer assignment, and unlike the round-2 cost reweighting it changes the arg-min by construction because it is added, not multiplied.
CHANGE: For every training item and every level, a hyperbolic Frechet mean of its training successors is pulled a curvature-determined fraction along the geodesic from the item, and the resulting point contributes an ADDITIVE bias to the item-code cost; the hard SID is then chosen by a capacity-exact deferred-acceptance pass whose per-code capacities are the Euclidean nearest-code counts, so the usage multiset is reproduced exactly while the membership, and therefore the gradient, is behaviour- and curvature-dependent.
SPECIFICATION: {'text': "Offline preprocessing (once, single process, CPU, TRAINING SPLIT ONLY):\n  T[i,j] = number of training sessions in which item j occurs in the position immediately after item i (window 1); p_i(j) = T[i,j]/sum_j T[i,j].\n  For each level l, take the frozen baseline prefix partition of the training items, build the quotient graph over codes, compute Ollivier curvature kappa_c (W1 between neighbour measures, unit edge lengths) and standardise against 20 member-shuffle nulls that preserve level sizes: z_l = (kappa_obs - mean_null)/sd_null, then centre over levels: delta_l = z_l - mean_l(z_l). The round-3 measured profile [-0.328,-0.071,+0.399] is the expected input.\n  t_l = sigmoid(delta_l) in (0,1); written as 3 floats into the Stage-2 config. TITLE: Capacity-conserving hyperbolic behaviour permutation of RQ-VAE SID triples (the triple bag is conserved; only the item->triple bijection is curved-and-behavioural)
MOTIVATION: The SID table that the generative recommender consumes is produced by a Euclidean arg-min. That arg-min ignores the training behaviour graph, so an item and its regular successors can land in unrelated prefixes, while the quantiser's capacity is allocated by embedding geometry alone. The two measured failures of the previous rounds were (i) curvature spent as a radius, which collapsed the codebook (170 -> 56 distinct triples, recall 0.041888) and (ii) a multiplicative per-pair weight, which moved costs but moved not a single arg-min. The problem this addresses is precisely that: how to make behaviour+curvature change the actual SID indices while the codebook's resolution is untouchable, i.e. frozen as a conserved quantity rather than merely "protected" by a soft plan or a clipped loss.
NOVELTY: No prior round in this repository changes the *pairing* between items and SID labels while conserving the label multiset. Previous arms moved code vectors (Poincare-Frechet codebook updates), set per-level scaling/radius from curvature (CURVCTRL-SID, BRad-RQ), added successor smoothing or successor boosting to the residual (LORENTZ-SUCCPROFILE-SMOOTH-RQ, succboost-geoshift), used MoE/cone branch structures (BRANCHCURV-MOEB-RQ, behcone-prefix-rq, TSG-SID) or solved an assignment/transport plan whose arg-max need not reproduce its marginals (CURVCAP-SUCCPLAN, refused). Here the object is a permutation of a fixed bag of whole triples, so the conservation is algebraic, not approximate; the cost is additively rank-fused (no weight to tune); and the measured standardised curvature deviation enters with the deliberately opposite sign to the round-1 arm (kappa_l = exp(+delta_l) instead of exp(-delta_l)), because the level whose behaviour quotient is *flatter* than its size-null is the level that needs the hyperbolic metric supplied, not the level that already has hierarchy.

Because every accepted move is a transposition, the multiset of triples is invariant, so per-level usage histograms, distinct-triple count and collision rate are exactly the baseline's.
